subject: face mite
title: Tiny Mites Crawl Out of Almost Every Adult's Face at Night

scenes.text: Tonight, while you sleep, tiny animals will crawl out of your face to mate.
They're face mites, a third of a millimetre long, living in the hair follicles of most adults.
By day they stay buried head first, eating the oil in your skin.
They've lost the genes that protect against sunlight, so they only come out in the dark.
Scientists think they even use your own sleep hormone, released at dusk, to wake up.
They've lived on us so long, they may be turning into part of us.

description:
Demodex folliculorum mites, about 0.3 mm long, live in the hair follicles of most adults' faces. A 2022 genome study led by the universities of Reading and Bangor found they have lost genes for UV protection and come out at night to mate.
The researchers suggest they may use the melatonin our skin releases at dusk, and could be shifting from parasites to symbionts.
Did you know these were living on you?
first_comment: Each mite has only a few hundred cells, and each leg runs on three single-cell muscles. Does this make you want to wash your face, or not think about it?
